title: Ultrasound-based breast nodule malignancy diagnosis using CNN enhanced by knowledge distillation

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Ultrasound-based breast nodule malignancy diagnosis using CNN enhanced by knowledge distillation》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0030】Breast cancer is one of the most prevalent malignant tumors among women worldwide and a major threat to women’s health and life safety.1,2,3 According to the latest statistical data from the World Health Organization (WHO) and the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), the incidence rate of breast cancer among women globally has surpassed that of lung cancer, ranking first, and shows an increasing trend year by year.4,5 Early screening and accurate diagnosis are considered crucial links to reduce the mortality rate of breast cancer and improve the cure rate.6 Traditional breast imaging examination methods include mammography, ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), etc.7 Each of these examinations has its own advantages and disadvantages: Mammography can display microcalcifications in the breast but has poor performance in imaging dense breasts8; MRI can provide high-resolution breast images but is expensive and complex to operate9; ultrasound, as a safe, economical, and non-radiative imaging method, is widely used in the early detection and follow-up of breast cancer due to its excellent imaging capability for dense breast tissue.10 However, ultrasound images have inherent limitations, such as severe noise interference, limited resolution, blurred boundaries, and imaging quality that is easily affected by the operator’s experience,11,12 leading to strong subjectivity and uncertainty in distinguishing benign from malignant breast lesions.13 These issues seriously affect the accuracy (Acc) of early breast cancer identification and benign-malignant diagnosis, especially for BI-RADS category 4 nodules, whose malignant detection rate varies widely (2%–95%), posing significant challenges to clinical diagnosis.14,15

【Introduction · p0035】In recent years, with the development of artificial intelligence (AI), deep learning (DL), and radiomics technologies, significant progress has been made in research on AI-assisted diagnosis of breast cancer based on medical imaging. Convolutional neural network (CNN) can automatically learn high-dimensional features from breast ultrasound images through multi-layer nonlinear feature extraction networks, enabling the detection and classification of lesion regions, which has significantly improved the Acc and consistency of diagnosis.16 Researchers have successfully applied models such as ResNet,17 DarkNet,18 and EfficientNet19 to the task of benign-malignant diagnosis of breast ultrasound images, and some results have reached or even exceeded the level of experienced radiologists.20 The Transformer architecture has also achieved breakthrough progress in the field of computer vision, and its self-attention mechanism can capture global dependency information and enhance feature expression capabilities.21 Networks based on vision transformer (ViT) and Swin Transformer have demonstrated comparable or even superior performance to CNN in the classification and segmentation of breast ultrasound images.22 Transformers can effectively integrate local and global information, showing significant advantages for tumor regions with complex morphologies and blurred boundaries. However, transformer models usually have large computational complexity, high requirements for data volume, and poor performance on small amounts of labeled data.

【Comparison with state-of-the-art methods · p0090】To further assess the generalization ability of the proposed model, external validation was performed on an independent private dataset that was not used during model training, and the results are summarized in Table 6. As shown in Table 6, the proposed model achieved the best performance, with an accuracy of 92.64%, precision of 92.56%, recall of 92.18%, F1-score of 92.37%, and AUC of 0.956. Compared with the other methods, our model consistently improved all evaluation metrics, demonstrating stronger feature representation and robustness under unseen data distributions. These results confirm the superior generalization capability and potential clinical applicability of the proposed approach. Figure 3 presents the confusion matrix of the proposed method on the external validation dataset, which provides a visual confirmation of its excellent classification performance and demonstrates accurate discrimination between benign and malignant lesions with limited misclassification. Despite the distribution differences between the public and private datasets, the proposed method maintained consistently superior classification performance, demonstrating its robustness and strong generalization ability. These findings further highlight the potential of the proposed framework for practical clinical applications in breast ultrasound image classification.

【Comparison with state-of-the-art methods · p0110】Considering the importance of computational efficiency for practical clinical deployment, we further evaluated the computational cost of the proposed model. As shown in Table 9, the proposed model achieved a favorable balance between computational efficiency and classification performance. It required only 4.12 M parameters and 0.32 G FLOPs, which were substantially lower than most CNN- and Transformer-based baseline models. Meanwhile, the proposed model achieved an inference latency of 7.38 ms and a peak memory consumption of 23.93 MB, demonstrating competitive inference efficiency and modest resource requirements. Although some lightweight models exhibited lower computational costs, they showed inferior classification performance. All latency and memory measurements were conducted under the same hardware and software environment described in the model training section. These results indicate that the proposed model achieves high classification performance with reduced computational burden, supporting its potential application in practical clinical scenarios.

【Performance metrics · p0315】The performance of the proposed model was comprehensively evaluated using the standard metrics defined in the quantification and statistical analysis section. To further illustrate the discriminative capability of the learned features, t-SNE visualization was first performed on the breast ultrasound datasets (Figure 1), demonstrating the separability of benign and malignant lesions in the learned feature space. Various CAM methods were then employed to visualize the regions contributing to the classification decisions (Figure 2). The confusion matrix on the external validation dataset (Figure 3) was subsequently presented to provide an intuitive overview of the classification results and misclassification patterns. Furthermore, the ROC curves of different models on the private dataset were compared (Figure 4), with the AUC values used to evaluate their discriminative performance. Finally, feature visualization and lesion localization results of different models were compared (Figure 5), highlighting the superior localization capability and interpretability of the proposed model.
